paragraphs: Mentioned in a baraita, Sanhedrin 7a [compare 4a], and in Sifra, Tazria, chapter 2. His students asked Rabbi Yehudah ben Ro'etz, ‘Shall I read “seventy”—’; he answered them, ‘He declared impure and pure in the case of male birth [supplied בוכר], etc.’

notes.text: The wording “seventy ... bokher” remains garbled and unresolved. The bounded Sanhedrin 7a lookup did not locate the quotation, and the attempted Sifra reference failed to resolve; neither supplies positive proof or a corrected quotation.

Two saved whole Davidson Sanhedrin4a scalars explicitly have Rabbi Yehudah ben Roetz and his students’ question about reading seventy. Supplied7a remains alongside4a. The source’s abbreviated question and dash are preserved rather than importing the full female-birth question into Hyman’s quotation. Supplied בוכר stays visible beside contextual male birth; no printed-letter history is established. SifraTazriachapter2 was not newly inspected, and failed earlier requests do not prove absence.

Sifra, Tazria, Parashat Yoledet 2:2 and Sanhedrin 4a both give the students’ question about reading “seventy” and the comparison with male birth. The photographed Hyman notice cites Sanhedrin 7a, abbreviates the exchange, and appears to read בזכר at the point represented by בוכר in the supplied transcription.
